metadata.note: The Manchester and Lawrence Railroad: a single ~28-mile line from Lawrence MA to Manchester NH, opened 13 Nov 1849 as a second Manchester - Boston route via the Boston and Maine. The M&L owned the New Hampshire portion; the 3.6-mi Massachusetts section was B&M-built and leased to it. It ran its own trains only briefly (1849-1850 and, less certainly, 1853-1856); the Concord Railroad operated it 1850-1853 and 1856-30 June 1887, and the Boston and Maine from 1887 (lease from 1 Sept 1887, merger 1 Jan 1919) until regular passenger service ended in 1953. Seasonal race specials ran Lawrence - Rockingham Park until 1960. Per CLAUDE.md Rule 4 the main line is drawn as three features sharing identical geometry, one per operator (the M&L and Concord features each carry two segments with a gap), plus a B&M race-special feature over the south end. NOT operator changes, deliberately not split on: the 1890 Concord & Montreal formation, the 1895 B&M lease of the C&M, the 1919 merger and the 1889 Concord-B&M settlement. Freight after 1953 is mentioned in notes only (Rule 1). Not drawn: the Hooksett Branch and Suncook Valley Extension (operated by others), the Nashua & Rochester crossing at Windham Junction, the Massachusetts Northeastern trolleys to Canobie Lake, and B&M buses on the corridor.

not_yet_sourced: Exact last day of regular passenger service: 1953 is year-level from Karr (1995) and Lindsell (2000); the primary floor is the Jan 1952 Official Guide. 'July 10, 1953' is unverified.

Operator 1853-1856: M&L per Nashua City Station (ICC valuation) and de.Wikipedia lease dates; the M&L's own 1888 bill says in summary the Concord ran it continuously 'since 1850'. Sources disagree; both readings recorded. The conservative alternative is one Concord era 1850-1887.
Who physically ran the trains 1 July - 31 Aug 1887 (M&L in possession with its own timetable; B&M lease dated 1 Sept). Folded into the B&M era; does not change any drawn year.

Rockingham Park race specials 1954-1960: secondary sources only; no primary timetable seen; whether they ran every season is not established. The 1935 racetrack spur's length and route are unknown and it is not drawn.
Headways 1849-1912 have no count at all; 1913 (6 round trips), 1934 (3) and 1952 (1) are the only counts, and everything between is interpolation.
Manchester Union Station (1898) site is not drawn; the line ends at the M&L's own depot area by Depot Street.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 2026-10-15 with opstrace.py over OpenStreetMap (maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror) plus OpenHistoricalMap. The router took the OpenHistoricalMap ways named 'Manchester & Lawrence Railroad' (OHM ways 200026110, 200026128, 200053626-200053632, start_date 1849) for the whole run: 27.2 mi of track, 100% on ways attributed to the M&L, no straight-line legs. Checked against the surviving OSM rail-trail ways tagged old_railway_operator=B&M (Methuen Rail Trail, Salem Bike-Ped Corridor, Windham Rail Trail, Derry Rail Trail, Londonderry Rail Trail, South Manchester Trail): the OHM line lies a mean 2-5 m and at most ~20-36 m from them. Documented mileage: 27.9 mi Lawrence - Manchester (J. Fowler, New Hampshire Railroads table 15); 27.2 mi from the Jan 1952 Official Guide (Lawrence 26.0 / Manchester 53.2 from Boston); de.Wikipedia ~44 km (27.3 mi). Traced 27.2 mi, within 3% of all three; trace mileposts match Fowler's at Windham (12.9 vs 12.9) and Derry (16.0 vs 16.1). NOT backed by any surviving OSM feature (drawn from OHM's historical mapping alone, no OSM corroboration): about 0.9 mi through Manchester-Boston Regional Airport (trace mi ~22.5-23.4), where the grade was sold and built over by a runway extension c.2000, plus several short urban pieces of 0.2-0.4 mi in Lawrence/Methuen (mi 0.7-1.1, 3.3-3.6) and Londonderry/airport approaches (mi 17.4-17.6, 20.0-21.5). Terminals: the south end is the OHM junction with the B&M Western Route at South Lawrence (42.6964 N, 71.1617 W), south of the Merrimack; per OHM the line crossed the Merrimack on its own bridge at about 42.701 N and ran north through North Lawrence (Essex St, trace mi 0.9). The 1931-2005 consolidated Lawrence station and the pre-1931 South Lawrence depot on the Western Route are not drawn as separate stubs. The north end is the OHM end of the M&L at its junction with the Concord main line beside Depot Street, Manchester (42.9853 N, 71.4659 W) -- the M&L's own depot area; trains from 1898 continued roughly half a mile up the Concord main to Manchester Union Station, which is not drawn because neither OSM nor OHM pins that station's site. Alignment era: this is the line's final (pre-abandonment) alignment as mapped in OHM; no source consulted documents a relocation since 1849, but the 1849-1887 eras are drawn on that later alignment and any early-era realignment would not show.

segments.note: Opened 13 November 1849 (Hurd 1882: 'opened Nov. 13, 1849'; de.Wikipedia: passengers from 13 Nov 1849, freight from 1 Jan 1850). Built by Manchester businessmen as a second Manchester - Boston route via the Boston and Maine at Lawrence. The 3.6-mi Massachusetts section (South Lawrence - Methuen - state line) was built and owned by the B&M (opened Aug 1849) and leased to the M&L; no source says passenger trains used it before 13 Nov 1849. Operated by the M&L itself ('Rail Operations 1849-1850', Nashua City Station from the 1931 ICC valuation) until the Concord Railroad lease of 1 Nov 1850. Headway is an estimate: no timetable count for this era was found.
sources: Segment-level: opening date from Hurd, History of Rockingham and Strafford Counties (1882) ch. VI and de.Wikipedia (Bahnstrecke Manchester-Lawrence, citing Lindsell 2000); M&L self-operation 1849-1850 from Nashua City Station (ICC valuation 1931); end at the 1 Nov 1850 Concord lease from de.Wikipedia. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: Second spell of M&L self-operation, between the end of the first Concord Railroad lease (1 Nov 1853) and the second (1 Dec 1856), per Nashua City Station ('Rail Operations ... 1853-1856', from the ICC valuation) and de.Wikipedia's lease dates. THE OPERATOR FOR THESE YEARS IS THE LEAST CERTAIN PART OF THIS LAYER: the M&L's own 1888 bill in equity says in its summary that the Concord operated the road 'since 1850, and down to July 1, 1887', though the same report dates the Concord's possession 'from 1856 thenceforward', which fits this gap. Passenger service itself is not in doubt -- the line ran under one operator or the other. Headway is an estimate: no timetable count for this era was found.
sources: Segment-level: operator from Nashua City Station (ICC valuation 1931) and de.Wikipedia lease dates, in tension with the M&L v. Concord bill as reported in the Independent Statesman, 1 Mar 1888. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: First Concord Railroad lease, 1 Nov 1850 - 1 Nov 1853 (de.Wikipedia). The Concord ran the M&L with its own Concord - Manchester main line, giving Concord - Manchester - Lawrence - Boston service over the B&M. The M&L's 1888 bill against the Concord confirms Concord operation 'since 1850'. Headway is an estimate: no timetable count for this era was found.
sources: Segment-level: lease dates from de.Wikipedia (Manchester and Lawrence Railroad); Concord operation from 1850 from the M&L v. Concord bill (New-York Tribune 28 Feb 1888; Independent Statesman 1 Mar 1888). Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: Second Concord Railroad era: lease from 1 Dec 1856 (de.Wikipedia); the formal lease expired 1 Aug 1867 but the Concord kept operating the road under continuing agreements until 30 June 1887 -- the M&L 'obtained possession of its railroad, July 1, 1887' (M&L bill in equity, Independent Statesman 1 Mar 1888). The Concord used the M&L's Manchester depots and rolling stock. The Concord became the Concord & Montreal only on 1 Jan 1890, after losing the M&L, so there is no Concord & Montreal era on this line. On regaining possession the M&L issued its own public timetable, 'Summer Arrangement, July 1, 1887' (The Henry Ford 89.0.633.132); who physically ran the trains in July-August 1887 is unresolved and is folded into the B&M era. Headway is an estimate: no timetable count for this era was found.
sources: Segment-level: lease and end dates from de.Wikipedia and the M&L v. Concord bill (Independent Statesman 1 Mar 1888; New-York Tribune 28 Feb 1888); M&L July 1887 timetable at The Henry Ford. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: B&M operation from 1887: M&L stockholders voted a 50-year lease to the B&M on 22 June 1887 and B&M stockholders ratified it the same day (New-York Tribune and Portland Daily Press, 23 Jun 1887); a B&M man was roadmaster of the 'Manchester & Lawrence division' by 27 Aug 1887 (Portland Daily Press); lease dated from 1 Sept 1887 (ICC valuation via Nashua City Station); NH Senate ratified it Oct 1887. Still the B&M's in 1892 (Weekly Union, Manchester, 26 Oct 1892), so the 1895 B&M lease of the Concord & Montreal was not an operator change here. Merged into the B&M 1 Jan 1919 (paper transaction, same operator). Headway estimated from the Nov 1913 count (six weekday round trips); no count for 1887-1912 was found.
sources: Segment-level: operator change from Chronicling America newspapers 1887 and 1892 and the ICC valuation via Nashua City Station; 1913 service level from de.Wikipedia citing the Nov 1913 Official Guide. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: Nov 1913 Official Guide (B&M Table 45, p.195, via de.Wikipedia citing Lindsell 2000): six weekday and four Sunday round trips, 53-68 minutes, all connecting at Lawrence for Boston. The 1913 count sets this headway; how and when service fell to the 1934 level is not known, so the figure for the later years of this span is an estimate. The 1935 Rockingham Park racetrack specials over the south end fall inside the regular service drawn here.
sources: Segment-level: service level from de.Wikipedia (Bahnstrecke Manchester-Lawrence) citing the Nov 1913 Official Guide; years between 1913 and 1934 interpolated. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: Feb 1934 Official Guide (B&M Table 35, p.80, via de.Wikipedia): three weekday and one Sunday round trip plus an early weekday Methuen - Lawrence train, with B&M buses running alongside (buses are not drawn). Headway from the 1934 count; the decline to one round trip by 1952 is not dated, so this figure is an estimate for the later years.
sources: Segment-level: service level from de.Wikipedia citing the Feb 1934 Official Guide; years between 1934 and 1952 interpolated. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

segments.note: Official Guide Feb 1952, B&M Table 37 'Manchester and Lawrence Branch' dated 7 Jan 1952: almost all bus columns, but one rail train each way (No. 1511 northbound, No. 1502 southbound); Derry and Methuen indexed to Table 37 with no freight dagger. That is the PRIMARY floor: rail service is primary-confirmed only to Jan 1952. The 1953 end is year-level from two published books -- Karr, Rail Lines of Southern New England (1995), via en.Wikipedia ('Passenger service on the Manchester and Lawrence ended in 1953'), and Lindsell (2000), via de.Wikipedia ('July 1953', latterly one gas-electric railcar each way on weekdays). A 'July 10, 1953' date attributed to Nashua City Station could not be found on any NCS page and is unverified. Do not extend past 1953 without evidence; north of Rockingham Park the line was freight-only afterwards (Salem - Derry out of service 1980, abandonments 1984-2001).
sources: Segment-level: Jan 1952 train from the Feb 1952 Official Guide (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, Table 37); 1953 end from Karr 1995 via en.Wikipedia and Lindsell 2000 via de.Wikipedia. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt

properties.speed_source: estimated: Nov 1913 Official Guide (B&M Table 45, via de.Wikipedia citing Lindsell 2000) gives 53-68 min for the ~28-mi Lawrence - Manchester run, i.e. about 40-51 km/h; 45 km/h taken as a mid value and applied to all eras without evidence for the others

properties.geometry_quality: The first 5.9 trace-miles of the same Manchester - Lawrence trace (from the South Lawrence junction with the B&M Western Route), cut at the point on the line nearest the Rockingham Park racetrack site (42.7686 N, 71.2204 W; the track site, now The Mall at Rockingham Park, lies about 0.4 mi west). J. Fowler's New Hampshire Railroads table 15 puts Rockingham Park at MP 4.5; his mileposts appear to count from Lawrence station north of the Merrimack, about 1.4 mi up the trace from the South Lawrence junction, so MP 4.5 falls at trace-mile ~5.9 - consistent with this cut. The B&M's 1935 racetrack spur is NOT drawn: its length is not established and neither OSM nor OHM shows it. No straight-line legs. Same OHM source and same terminal caveat at Lawrence as the main-line features.

segments.note: After regular service ended in 1953, seasonal B&M race specials - mostly through from Boston via the Western Route to Lawrence - continued over the south end of the line to Rockingham Park racetrack (opened 1935; B&M spur built 1935), 'until 1960' (en.Wikipedia; J. Fowler 'Rockingham Park (1935>1960) #(races)', the # marking dates from histories, not a timetable; de.Wikipedia 'bis 1960 von Sonderzuegen'). Year-level, secondary only: no primary race-special timetable or notice was found for any year 1954-1960, and whether specials ran every season is not established. Headway is nominal -- specials ran only on race days in season. Lawrence - Rockingham Park was freight-only after the 1960 season (to 1999).
sources: Segment-level: 1960 end from en.Wikipedia, J. Fowler New Hampshire Railroads table 15 and de.Wikipedia (Lindsell 2000); no primary source found. Researched in research/branches/manchester_and_lawrence_railroad.txt
